doc_name: Why Do They Call Me Mr. Happy?
text: Why Do They Call Me Mr. Happy? is the sixth full-length album by Vancouver punk rock group Nomeansno, released in 1993. It is their second album recorded by the original two-piece lineup of brothers Rob and John Wright, following their 1982 debut album Mama, and the first after the departure of longtime guitarist Andy Kerr. The album marks a shift from their hardcore punk roots to slower songs influenced by heavy metal and progressive rock. Critics praised it for its balance of heaviness and subtlety, highlighting the dynamics of the band in its original form. The Wright brothers formed Nomeansno in 1979 as a two-piece, initially making home recordings and later rehearsing as a bass-and-drums duo; their self-released 1982 debut, Mama, features material from this era. In 1983, Andy Kerr joined, leading to the band signing with Alternative Tentacles and releasing four albums and several EPs. Kerr left after touring late in 1991 and moved to the Netherlands. The Wright brothers then focused on their Ramones-influenced side project The Hanson Brothers, while Rob began working on solo material under the name Mr. Wrong. In February 1993, the brothers began working on the album; Rob Wright, the band's bassist, also played guitar during recording sessions. Demo tracks were recorded at Dollhouse Studio, with final versions recorded at Cecil English's Profile Sound Studios. The album was engineered by Brian Else, produced by Nomeansno, and mixed by Else, Nomeansno, and longtime roadie Craig Bougie. The band experimented in the studio, and the final track, "Cats, Sex, and Nazis," includes audio samples of Faith No More's "We Care a Lot," songs by The Residents, Deep Purple, and a previously released Nomeansno song, "I Am Wrong." Three of the ten songs—“I Need You,” “Cats, Sex, and Nazis,” and “Happy Bridge”—were originally written during Kerr's time with the band: the first two were outtakes from sessions for the previous album, 0 + 2 = 1, and the latter was initially a demo; these versions were later released on the 0 + 2 = 1 ½ retrospective compilation. Of the seven other tracks on the album, four—“The Land of the Living,” “The River,” “Machine,” and “Lullaby”—were taken from the Mr. Wrong project, with the rest being new compositions. Four outtakes from these sessions were later included on the compilation Mr. Right & Mr. Wrong: One Down & Two to Go. Alternative Tentacles released the album in 1993 as a ten-track CD and seven-track LP, with the LP including only tracks 1 through 6 and 10. For the supporting tour, the Wright brothers expanded Nomeansno to include guitarist Tom Holliston and second drummer Ken Kempster, both from The Hanson Brothers; Holliston remained with the band until their 2016 breakup and later called Why Do They Call Me Mr. Happy? his favorite Nomeansno record. The album fell out of print when Nomeansno acquired the rights to their back catalogue from Alternative Tentacles, and despite reissuing many records on their Wrong Records imprint, Why Do They Call Me Mr. Happy? has not been reissued. The album received positive critical reception and became a fan favorite; John Doran of The Guardian called it "the high watermark of western civilization" in a 2016 retrospective review, while AllMusic critic Ned Raggett praised it for reaching "amazing rock epic heights" with "sheer lift and charge," highlighting its power and subtlety and awarding it 4.5 out of 5 stars. Jan Jaedike of Rock Hard magazine described it as a challenging listen due to its heaviness and repetition but ultimately rewarding, giving it 7.5 out of 10 stars. All songs on the album were written by Nomeansno, except tracks 5, 7, and 10, which were co-written by Nomeansno and Andy Kerr. Note: the track listing refers to the CD issue (1993, Alternative Tentacles).
